rules.rule:
This is an MCP server acting as ONE person's on-premises Exchange mailbox through EWS (SOAP). It is its own OAuth 2.1 server and seals the person's credential (an AD FS refresh token, or in password mode the directory password) into the tokens it issues. Report each of the following as a blocking finding, quoting the line:

1. HTTP (httpx, requests, aiohttp, urllib) or a SOAP request (M./T. element builders, XML strings) outside src/exchange_mcp/ews/. The only other HTTP allowed: AD FS in src/exchange_mcp/auth/adfs.py, the Vault/OpenBao transit client in src/exchange_mcp/keys/vault.py, the outbound client factory in src/exchange_mcp/app.py, and the link routes in src/exchange_mcp/links/routes.py. The initial EWS allowlist in ews/client.py is the design; report only additions to it.
2. A function or tool argument that selects a mailbox, user or server; an ExchangeImpersonation header; a Mailbox/EmailAddress element for anyone but the signed-in person in a mailbox operation (GetUserAvailability and ResolveNames are the exceptions); a URL built from user input.
3. Key material read from os.environ / os.getenv; a password, token, key or login passed to a logger, put in an exception message, a URL, or a tool result.
4. A credential, session or draft persisted to a database, file or shared cache.
5. verify=False, ssl.CERT_NONE, an http:// upstream, or a config path that yields them.
6. A code path that sends mail (SendItem, MessageDisposition SendOnly/SendAndSaveCopy), sends meeting invitations/updates/cancellations (SendToAll*, SendToChanged*, CancelCalendarItem) or sets an automatic reply on, WITHOUT checking user_confirmed is True and drawing from the bucket before the EWS call.
7. DeleteType other than MoveToDeletedItems; EmptyFolder; MessageDisposition other than SaveOnly outside send_draft.
8. Inbox rules (GetInboxRules/UpdateInboxRules), forwarding, delegates (AddDelegate etc.), folder permissions, other or shared mailboxes, ExportItems, SyncFolderItems/SyncFolderHierarchy, Subscribe/GetEvents/GetStreamingEvents, public folders; any new entry in the EWS operation allowlist.
9. A tool result built from an EWS object without a projection; ChangeKey, ItemClass or ResponseCode reaching a result.
10. A list without a hard cap of 25, an offset argument, or truncation without a truncated flag.
11. Bytes or base64 in a tool result.
12. An exception converted to a successful return, or a result dict with an 'error' key.
13. Tool annotations contradicting behaviour.
14. Outgoing HTML not passed through the html pipeline (sanitize -> cid images -> inline css -> validate).
15. A reply/forward built by replacing a body instead of ReplyToItem/ReplyAllToItem/ForwardItem.
16. Seal or signed-link verification with == instead of hmac.compare_digest / AES-GCM tag check; a sealer that accepts an empty or short key; a field outside the signature or the AES-GCM associated data.
17. A whole file read into memory without a size bound.
18. Sign-in password checking without the attempt limiter, or with different responses for unknown login vs wrong password.

Non-blocking: comments that explain what instead of why; non-English text; duplicated helpers that exist in src/exchange_mcp/core/.

Tool definitions. Additionally report: a tool name not starting with list_, get_, save_, delete_ or an explicit verb (send_, cancel_, respond_, update_, find_); a prefix such as exchange_, ews_ or mcp_; a description shorter than three sentences or one that only restates the name; an irreversible tool whose description does not say it cannot be undone; nested object arguments where a scalar or list of scalars works; an action argument typed as str instead of a Literal enum; an argument whose name is not self-explanatory but has no description.

Tests. Report: a test that calls a real Exchange or AD FS without the 'live' pytest marker; a test with no assertion or that asserts only that no exception was raised; a negative-scenario test that does not assert isError, the error text and that no EWS write happened; a streaming test whose fake does not reproduce the stream being closed; a test that would still pass if the behaviour it names were removed; a real hostname, domain, address or person's name in a fixture.
